core.headline: End-of-terrace Victorian cottage, Smarden
core.summary: A two-bedroom end-of-terrace Victorian cottage in Smarden with cast-iron fireplace, quarry-tiled kitchen floor and cottage garden. Guide Price £425,000 freehold. Within the conservation area.
core.listing:
An end-of-terrace Victorian cottage built circa 1880, constructed of red brick under a clay-tiled roof. The cottage has two bedrooms and stands on The Street in the centre of Smarden.

The sitting room measures 3.90m x 3.60m (12'10" x 11'10") and has a cast-iron fireplace. The kitchen/dining room measures 4.30m x 3.20m (14'1" x 10'6") and has a quarry-tiled floor, reclaimed beams and a range alcove. Ledged-and-braced doors are fitted throughout the ground floor.

On the first floor, bedroom one measures 3.80m x 3.30m (12'6" x 10'10") and bedroom two measures 2.90m x 2.40m (9'6" x 7'10"). There is one bathroom. Head height at the top of the stairs is restricted to approximately 1.88m (6'2").

To the rear is a cottage garden of approximately 12m (40ft) with a brick path and timber shed.

Smarden village has a pub approximately 2 minutes' walk from the cottage. Parking is on-street.

Guide Price £425,000. Freehold. Council Tax Band C (Ashford Borough Council). EPC rating E. The property is within the Smarden Conservation Area. The septic tank is shared with 1 Forge Cottages and located in its garden; access rights for maintenance; emptying costs shared. The rear of the garden is in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded. The seller does not know whether the shared septic tank meets the Environment Agency's 2020 general binding rules. Restricted head height at top of stairs, approximately 1.88m (6'2").
keyFeatures: Quarry-tiled kitchen floor with range alcove and reclaimed beams
Cottage garden approx. 12m (40ft) with brick path and shed
Septic tank shared with no. 1; emptying costs shared
